category: relay/P2P — SIGNALLING with encrypted fallback transport

free_tier.stated: iroh includes a set of public relays provided by n0.computer, available to all iroh users at no cost.

retention.stated: Relays are stateless and store nothing; no retention period applies to relayed traffic.
retention.notes: unverified: no data retention period stated for relayed traffic

egress.terms: Public relays are free, open to every iroh endpoint, and rate-limited to prevent abuse of shared infrastructure.

interface_detail: An iroh connection is just a QUIC connection, using TLS and TLS ALPNs for protocol negotiation.
tooling: `iroh` crate; relay is a library, not a service with an upload endpoint
chaining: In practice, roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a stepping stone.

limits.value: unverified: Community rate is Variable; 5 MB/s belongs to the Pro shared-relay tier
unverified: Community connections are Rate limited; 10,000 belongs to the Pro shared-relay tier

limits_note: Not a storage provider. Only relayed bytes hit the operator, hence the per-connection rate limit rather than a byte quota.
reliability_note: 'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed' and 'Do not rely on it for production workloads'. The free tier is explicitly capacity-unstable by design.
confidence_note: the public relays are stated as free to all iroh users on the Public Relays page

evidence.proved: relays do not store routed traffic
evidence.quote: Because relays are stateless (they route encrypted packets but store nothing), they're cheap to run and easy to scale.

evidence.proved: public relays are available to all users at no cost
evidence.quote: iroh includes a set of public relays provided by n0.computer, available to all iroh users at no cost. No setup required; they work out of the box.

evidence.proved: public relays need no account or authentication
evidence.quote: Public relays are open to every iroh endpoint and need no authentication.

evidence.proved: the public relays are explicitly not for production workloads
evidence.quote: This means that public infrastructure is meant for development and hobby use. Do not rely on it for production workloads, especially if your application is sensitive to rate limiting, uptime, or relay software version.

notes: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.
binding_note: one stream is shaped, and aggregate throughput is the shaped rate times the number of streams
